newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares end week mixed in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares end week mixed in Beirut.

text.p: Bank shares were mixed in the week ended on Friday on the Beirut Stock Exchange with Bank Audi rising to $16.125 from $15.875 last week and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce down to $12 from $12.25.
"Audi is a good buy. It initialled the real opening of the banking sector to investors," a dealer, who wished not to be identified, told Reuters.
Shares in Audi began trading at $15 on January 20 while BLC shares first traded at $11.25 on December 30.
Solidere A shares -- distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district Solidere is rebuilding -- held steady at $10.75.
B shares -- issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994 -- rose to $11 from $10.625 last Friday.
"As long as Solidere A shares are still being distributed to former holders of property rights, I don't expect much to happen on the market," the dealer said.
He expected intervention with blocs of demand orders to keep steady the Solidere share prices during the coming six to eight months.
Uniceramic shares changed hands on Friday at $1.5 for the first time since last June. Last November, the BSE suspended the pricing of the shares after the company increased its capital.
Kamil Saade, Financial Manager at Uniceramic told Reuters the firm's total equity of six billion pounds was increased to 15 billion late last year.

"The increase came from reserves after the revaluation of fixed assets. The company's new total equity of 15 billion pounds was divided by the existing number of shares and the new share price was obtained," he added.
Market sources said Uniceramic shares were trading on the grey market at $1.33 after the capital increase. On June 14, they traded at $3.25 on the BSE.

Total weekly turnover in all traded shares on the BSE was 567,427 shares from 541,896 last week. Turnover was 189,200 shares a week earlier. Total value of shares traded on the floor rose to $6,974,064 from $4,181,141.
There was no trade in the three other firms listed on the BSE: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit.
The BLOM stock index rose by 1.46 percent on the week to 918.26.
